paragraphs: Royal dress was regulated by law for centuries: who could wear fur, which fur, and how much of it. That is why a fur trimmed robe still reads as authority rather than as warmth, and why the costume does most of the character work before the face is even seen.
The figure is supplied with fur on the garment and holds CheckMate Lite and Pro certification. A rigged build of the same character is offered separately.

At $149 it suits historical and period visualisation, film and television, game characters, book and editorial illustration, and theatre previsualisation. On sale since 2015, which makes it one of the oldest listings in the library.

The LCVP is the boat with the ramp at the front, and the reason every film about an amphibious landing looks the way it does. The design is brutally simple: a shallow hull that can run itself onto a beach, drop the bow, unload and reverse off before it is stuck.

The model holds 320,831 polygons and 333,893 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification, and the library carries a substantial range around it, including Mk5 builds, rigged versions with native rigs for Maya and Cinema 4D, and a build supplied with soldiers aboard.
At $149 it suits military and naval visualisation, documentary and historical work, film and television, simulation and game environments. On sale since 2025.

The Triple E class ships changed the shape of container vessels: the bridge moved forward, the engine room moved aft, and everything between became cargo. Loaded, the stacks rise well above the deckhouse, and the ship becomes a moving wall.

The model is dense at 1,863,210 polygons and 2,066,912 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplied loaded. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and the library also holds the empty version, an ultra large container vessel, a deckhouse, a lifeboat and its davit crane as separate pieces.
At $149 it suits shipping and logistics visualisation, port and infrastructure scenes, documentary and news graphics, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2021.

A hypersonic launcher spends almost all of its life as a trailer. Erected and loaded, the canisters go vertical and the vehicle stops looking like transport at all, which is the only configuration in which the system is worth depicting.

The model holds 1,078,071 polygons and 1,188,141 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplied in the ready to fire configuration with the missiles loaded. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $149 it suits defence visualisation and presentation, documentary and news graphics, simulation, film and game environments, and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

Supplying the anatomy and the skin together answers a question a muscle map cannot: why the surface looks the way it does. The bulge, the hollow behind the knee, the line down the shin are all consequences of what sits underneath, and seeing both layers at once is what makes the connection.

The model holds 62,686 polygons and 62,958 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 65 maps, 2 at 8192x8192, 19 at 4096x4096, 31 at 2048x2048 and 13 at 1024x1024. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $149 it suits medical education and patient explanation, physiotherapy and sports science, anatomy reference for artists, and character work. On sale since 2020.

Bone is the one part of the body that survives everything, which is why teaching, forensics and art all start there. A collection gives the skeleton in more than one arrangement, and that is what turns it from an object into teaching material.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplied as static pieces. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.

At $149 the set suits medical and biology education, museum and exhibition work, anatomy reference for artists, forensic and archaeological visualisation, and game and film assets. On sale since 2016.

Streetwear is the clothing most people in a city are actually wearing, and that is precisely what architectural renders keep getting wrong by dressing everybody for the office. A hoodie and trainers date a scene to now rather than to nowhere.

The figure is very light at 7,753 polygons and 8,407 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, built for crowds and background use, but textured generously with 20 maps, 14 at 4096x4096, 2 at 3000x3000 and 4 at 1000x1000. It carries StemCell certification.
At $149 it suits architectural and urban visualisation, advertising and apparel imagery, game crowds, film previsualisation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2020.

An assassin's kit is a contradiction: armour where a blade might land, nothing where movement matters, and a hood doing the work a helmet would otherwise do. The design is always a compromise between being protected and being quiet.

The outfit holds 55,258 polygons and 54,930 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, which suits the repeated straps and plates, and is supplied in a T pose ready for your own rig. It carries StemCell certification.
At $149 it suits game characters, fantasy and historical film work, concept art, tabletop illustration and previsualisation. On sale since 2026.

The tavern is where every story of the period actually happens. Low beams, a fire, long tables built for strangers to share: it was the only heated room most people could enter without an invitation, which is why it became the setting for everything from bargains to brawls.
The scene holds 987,053 polygons and 1,008,520 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, covering the room and its fittings. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $149 it suits game environments, historical and period film sets, animation, museum and education work, and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

The Tourer is what happens when a van is fitted out for people instead of parcels: windows down both sides, proper seating and trim, and a role somewhere between a minibus and a shuttle. Hotels, airports and small tour operators run on exactly this vehicle.
The model holds 219,325 polygons and 245,125 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification. A rigged build is offered separately.
At $149 it suits street and architectural visualisation, transport and hospitality presentation, fleet mockups, advertising, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2021.

The Sprinter is the van that made the tall, narrow European shape normal everywhere else, including America. Standing room inside, a footprint that still parks, and a body available in enough lengths and heights that most trades never need anything else.

The model holds 514,878 polygons and 581,099 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 11 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and rigged builds are offered separately, including native rigs for Maya and Cinema 4D.
At $149 it suits street and architectural visualisation, fleet and livery mockups, logistics presentation, advertising, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2019.

The Met at Lincoln Center is a building designed around its own lobby. Five arches of glass, and behind them a staircase and chandeliers meant to be seen from the plaza, so the audience arriving becomes part of the performance for anyone outside.

The model is deliberately light at 27,260 polygons and 32,778 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, suited to city scenes where the building is one element among many. It carries StemCell certification.
At $149 it suits urban and architectural visualisation, cultural and tourism imagery, news and documentary graphics, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2024.

Self loading is the entire point of the palletized load system. A hook arm reaches back, drags a loaded flatrack onto the bed, and the truck drives away without a crane, a forklift or anybody standing in the open to help. In green rather than camouflage, it reads as a working vehicle rather than a front line one.
This is the light build, 11,664 polygons and 11,614 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout, made for convoys, background use and real time scenes. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $149 it suits military logistics visualisation, defence presentation, simulation, documentary and film, and game environments. On sale since 2026.

Bergen built the Bybanen because the city sits in a valley between mountains and could not widen a single road. A light rail line was the only way to move that many people, and the low floor articulated trams that run it are now as much a part of the city's image as the harbour.

The model holds 1,145,160 polygons and 1,189,523 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification, and rigged builds are offered separately, including native rigs for Cinema 4D and Maya.
At $149 it suits urban and transport visualisation, infrastructure presentation, architectural scenes, advertising, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2024.
